encounters.cc: Fall in bathroom with brief loss of consciousness; partner notes progressive clumsiness and hat no longer fits properly.

lines: Fall in bathroom with brief loss of consciousness; partner notes progressive clumsiness and hat no longer fits properly.

The patient is a 70-year-old male with a history of Paget disease of bone, upper urinary tract urothelial carcinoma, pellagra, and peripheral arterial disease who presents to the emergency department following a fall.
He reports that he tripped getting out of the shower and hit the back of his head on the tile.
His partner mentions that although he did not have a seizure, she has noticed he has been increasingly clumsy over the past few months.
The patient adds that his favorite hat no longer fits the way it used to, and he has had some occasional left-sided hearing loss.
He denies headache, diplopia, or focal weakness.
- Peripheral Arterial Disease with intermittent claudication (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Family history of alcohol use disorder
He has a 40-pack-year smoking history and drinks one glass of wine with dinner.
His temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), blood pressure is 142/80 mm Hg, and pulse is 76/min.
Physical examination reveals a prominent occipital ridge and mild sensorineural hearing loss in the left ear.
Non-contrast CT of the head shows no evidence of intracranial bleeding but does reveal irregular thickening and patchy sclerosis of the occipital bone with mixed radiolucent and radiodense areas.
